bullets: Game 3 of 6 in the video (video 556.7s-726.7s, 170 s readable), on the Hog/Earthquake cycle list, versus Giant/Sparky beatdown with Graveyard, Miner, Dark Prince, Earthquake and the Heroic Mega Minion: won on tower HP (own 1142/3652 versus enemy 161/572 at clock 0:03) - "Let's go. What a win, man" (710s).

The deck loses the first big exchange and he says so out loud: a Sparky beats his Skeletons + last-second Electro Spirit + Log at clock 1:57 and takes his left tower from 4360 to 1275. His stated adjustment at 1:55 is to stop trying to win the race - "when we get surprise factored like that, just not losing the game straight up is honestly enough to ask for" - and to chip the other lane with Hog Rider punishes instead (clock 1:49, 4351 -> 3844).

The win comes from one Mighty Miner sequence: bridged at (15, 12) at clock 1:14 as a pure read on a back-line Sparky with Cannon held in hand as insurance, then Explosive Escape at 1:10 to swap lanes on the opponent's half, supported by a speculative Log at (2, 14). The enemy left tower goes 4663 -> 161 between 1:03 and 0:57 - "Dude, he's in a really bad spot after that... what a reaction time. Yo, that was so fast."

The defensive pattern is stacking cheap cards rather than spending one big answer: against the Sparky + Graveyard + Dark Prince push from clock 0:57 to 0:34 he lays Cannon (8, 10), Skeletons (11, 14), Mighty Miner (7, 11) with an Electro Spirit reset, Firecracker (9, 6) in front of the King tower, Skeletons (6, 10), Evo Cannon (7, 8) with a second Electro Spirit, and The Log (4, 9) - holding on 1142 HP with the King activated: "I think we just saved our tower here. Nice, what a defense."

Closing pattern with a lead on HP: spend early instead of holding - "all we have to do is save our tower for another 20 seconds from a Sparky push. Let's firecracker early" (clock 0:22) - then cycle Hog Rider, Electro Spirit, Evo Firecracker and Skeletons into the opponent's half purely to keep them defending.

Earthquake is used exactly once and only as an opener: cast at clock 2:47 on the opponent's half at (14, 19), 1.5 s behind the bridge Hog Rider and in the same lane. No defensive Earthquake appears in the readable window; the eighth slot in the per-game HUD read came back as Heal Spirit on ~0.5-confidence hand reads with no deploy label, no unit track and no commentary, and is treated as noise.

new_deck.rationale: Average elixir 2.6 with Hog Rider as the only win condition, Earthquake as its spell partner, and Cannon, Skeletons, Electro Spirit and The Log as one- to three-elixir answers cycled repeatedly, with Mighty Miner as the single heavy card.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Six of the eight cards cost three elixir or less, so the deck answers a push by laying several cheap cards on top of each other instead of paying for one big answer - in this match a Sparky, Graveyard and Dark Prince push is held on 1142 HP with Cannon, Skeletons twice, Mighty Miner, Firecracker, two Electro Spirit resets and The Log. Hog Rider does not need a push behind it: it goes to the bridge on the opening play, with Earthquake dropped in the same lane 1.5 s later to strip the defending building, and again the instant the opponent commits elixir, so a beatdown deck is always paying to defend a lane it did not choose. Mighty Miner is the deck's swing card rather than a defensive tank - deployed at the bridge on a read that the opponent is placing a Sparky in the back, then Explosive Escape swaps him into the undefended lane, which took an enemy tower from 4663 to 161 HP in six seconds here. The weakness is equally visible: Electro Spirit is the only Sparky reset, and when the timing misses by a fraction the deck concedes a tower outright.
